chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from al-Mufaddal, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Seven hundred prophets have prayed in Masjid al-Khayf, and what is between the corner (of the Ka'ba) and the Maqam (Station of Ibrahim) is indeed fraught with the graves of the prophets, and Adam is truly in the sanctuary of God, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.الرُّكْن: al-Rukn — the corner of the Ka'ba containing the Black Stone (al-Hajar al-Aswad)
key_terms.الْحَرَم: al-Haram — the sacred sanctuary of Mecca, whose boundaries are inviolable
key_terms.الْمَقَام: al-Maqam — the Station of Ibrahim, the stone bearing the footprints of Prophet Ibrahim (AS)
key_terms.لَمَشْحُون: lam-shahhun — indeed fraught/loaded/full (emphatic lam + passive participle from sha-h-na)
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الْخَيْفِ: Masjid al-Khayf — the mosque in Mina (near Mecca) where many prophets are said to have prayed

ai.seo_question: How many prophets prayed in Masjid al-Khayf according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) reveals the profound sanctity of Mina's Masjid al-Khayf and the sacred precincts of Mecca. The Imam discloses that seven hundred prophets have performed salat in Masjid al-Khayf, and that the area between the Black Stone corner of the Ka'ba and the Station of Ibrahim is laden with the graves of prophets. Furthermore, the first prophet Adam (AS) rests within the Haram of God. This hadith situates hajj within a grand prophetic tradition reaching back to the very beginning of humanity, reminding pilgrims that they walk in the footsteps of countless messengers of God.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Al Mufazzal, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

Seven hundred Prophets<sup>as</sup> have Prayed in Masjid Al-Khief, and that what is in between the corner (of the Kaaba) and the Standing Place (of Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>) is fraught with the graves of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>, and that Adam<sup>as</sup> is in the Sanctuary of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Najran from al-Mufaddal from Jabir who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Seven hundred prophets said salat (prayer) in the Masjid of al-Khif, in Mina. The area between the corner and al-Maqam (the station of Ibrahim) is full of the graves of prophets; and Adam is in the Sacred place of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious.”
